note: Sezen, reading 1 gave you the map of self-regulation. This reading zooms in on one skill you use all the time: reading. A reader keeps asking herself whether she understands a text and rereads what she does not. The chapter shows that this loop is only as good as her judgment, and that most readers judge badly. The big question of these notes is: how can a reader judge her own understanding more accurately, and does that make her learn more?

The notes follow the seven steps of the reading 2 walk-through on your dashboard, as seven lectures. Lecture 2.1 sets out the model, 2.2 shows how accuracy is measured (Table 8.1), 2.3 why judgments go wrong, 2.4 and 2.5 the two ways to improve them, 2.6 whether better judgments pay off, and 2.7 what is still open and what teachers can do. Every lecture ends with the trap. The exam-style questions, memory hooks and games are on your dashboard and in the two Theme 3 practice sets.

friend: "When you read, you keep asking yourself whether you get it, and you reread what you don't. The catch is that most people are bad at that judgment: they go by how easy the text felt. Two things help: testing yourself a bit later, with a few keywords or a summary, and reading in a way that builds real understanding, like making your own concept map, explaining it to yourself, or knowing the test will ask you to explain. Then you pick the right texts to reread, and you actually understand more."
